title: On-Device Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech in Google AI Edge Gallery
gist: Google AI Edge adds fully on-device ASR and TTS to its AI Edge Gallery app, pairing compact speech models with on-device SLMs (Gemini Nano, Gemma 4) for offline voice AI. On Android, ML Kit system speech models transcribe 100+ languages at 10x real-time and a diffusion TTS starts speaking in ~100 ms with 0 MB APK cost; cross-platform, MediaPipe Tasks and LiteRT ship open-weight models like Parakeet-TDT 0.6B and Kokoro-82M.

themes.theme: On-device voice as the next AI interface

insights.claim: Google's AI Edge team argues recent advances in compact speech architectures make it possible to run accurate multilingual ASR and expressive TTS entirely on device, offline, with low latency and small memory, and pair them with on-device SLMs like Gemini Nano and Gemma 4.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Strengthens the edge-AI thesis: voice assistants that need no cloud inference shift compute cost to devices and favor phone/wearable silicon vendors.
insights.quote: Voice is often the most natural way to interact with AI on phones and wearables.
insights.locator: Today, we are introducing on-device Automatic

insights.claim: Google chose a modular cascade of separate lightweight ASR/TTS models with language models, rather than relying on multimodal models like Gemma 4 that can process audio directly, for latency optimization and flexibility.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Indicates end-to-end multimodal audio is not yet the efficient default on device; specialized small speech models retain a role.
insights.locator: While multimodal models like Gemma 4 can process audio

insights.claim: The XR Language Teacher showcase runs vision, language and speech models 100% locally on a phone: the user points the camera at an object or menu, speaks a question, and on-device ASR streams it with the camera frame to Gemini Nano (Android) or Gemma 4 (other platforms) in a single pass.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Demonstrates offline multimodal use cases (travel, no connectivity) that cloud assistants cannot serve.
insights.locator: Live visual grounding and streaming voice input

insights.claim: The model uses a structured output schema that tags foreign-language phrases separately, letting the TTS pipeline switch voices and accents mid-sentence for bilingual code-switching.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: A practical pattern for language-learning and translation apps built on small local models.
insights.locator: Structured outputs for bilingual TTS code-switching

insights.claim: Because inference runs on a paired phone, the Language Teacher experience extends to hands-free smart glasses, which Google presented at Android Dev Summit.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Points to phone-tethered intelligent eyewear as a target form factor for Google's on-device AI stack.

insights.claim: Google's ML Kit GenAI Speech Recognition delivers multilingual ASR across 100+ languages at 8.0% to 9.0% Word Error Rate on FLEURS, transcribing 10x faster than real time (~300 ms per 3 seconds of speech) and cutting end-to-end speech translation wait times by 35% to 44%.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Hard benchmark numbers for system-level on-device ASR that third-party speech API vendors must compete against.
insights.quote: reaching 8.0% to 9.0% Word Error Rate on FLEURS
insights.locator: ML Kit GenAI Speech Recognition API

insights.claim: ML Kit's on-device TTS uses a compact few-step diffusion model accelerated on NPU that starts speaking in ~100 ms, generates 24 kHz speech across 8 voices and 21 locales at up to 50x real-time, synthesizes a 27-second paragraph in ~500 ms, and cuts active device power by over 50% versus traditional autoregressive TTS.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Diffusion-based TTS with large power savings is a notable efficiency shift that undercuts cloud TTS economics for mobile apps.
insights.quote: cutting active device power by over 50% compared to traditional autoregressive TTS models

insights.claim: ML Kit speech models are integrated into Android and managed through AICore and Google's on-device speech services, adding 0 MB to an app's APK and receiving background model updates plus NPU/TPU hardware acceleration when available.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: OS-level bundling gives Google a distribution moat against standalone speech SDKs on Android.
insights.locator: Building for flagship Android with ML Kit

themes.theme: Cross-platform open-weight stack: MediaPipe and LiteRT

insights.claim: For iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and Web, MediaPipe Tasks provides turnkey ASR and TTS APIs that handle audio framing, Voice Activity Detection and decoding, with streaming, batch and hybrid transcription modes.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Google is extending its on-device AI tooling beyond Android to capture cross-platform developers.
insights.locator: Building across platforms with MediaPipe Tasks

insights.claim: Google optimized open-weight speech bundles in the .litertlm format, including Parakeet-TDT 0.6B (multilingual ASR), PocketTTS 100M, Kokoro-82M and Phonon 31M, with Phonon 31M achieving sub-100ms time-to-first-audio on most devices.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Very small open-weight speech models (31M-600M params) running in real time broaden the competitive field beyond proprietary speech APIs.

insights.claim: LiteRT, Google's on-device inference infrastructure that powers both ML Kit and MediaPipe Tasks, packages all speech model subgraphs and assets (encoders/decoders, tokenizers, phonemizers, vocoders) into a single .litertlm file for deployment.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: A unified deployment format is a platform play to make LiteRT the default runtime for edge models.
insights.locator: Speech models often rely on multiple subgraphs

insights.claim: The Hugging Face LiteRT Community, with over 10K followers, offers a growing catalog of open-weight speech models such as Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, Moonshine, Qwen3-TTS and Matcha.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Shows Google courting the open-model ecosystem, including Alibaba's Qwen models, to grow LiteRT adoption.
insights.locator: Speech models often rely on multiple subgraphs

insights.claim: Google's reference code schedules TTS synthesis at the sentence level, strips Markdown and skips code and tables, to avoid compute and memory contention during LLM token generation on device.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Resource contention between concurrent on-device models is a real constraint that shapes edge AI hardware requirements.
insights.locator: Reference implementation for chat voice outputs

insights.claim: Developers can test and benchmark on-device voice pipelines across 200+ real physical devices in Google Cloud's Developer Device Platform, and the Gallery app with the new features is available on Android and iOS.
insights.speaker: SF
insights.so_what: Device fragmentation remains a hurdle for edge AI, which Google is monetizing via cloud device testing.
insights.locator: Start building with ML Kit, MediaPipe Tasks, and LiteRT
